citations.assessment: Names Elazar of Bartota and his giving maxim.
Both consecutive mishnayot preserve the Yehoshua attribution.
The baraita puts the ruling in Yehoshua’s name and the later passage returns to those rulings.
Names Elazar son of Rabbi Yehudah of Bartota transmitting Yehoshua. Akiva adds a separate received ruling.
The checked Mishnah reads Rabban Gamliel, while Heilprin and Zakut report Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. Preserve the distinction.
The story names Elazar of Birta. It describes collectors hiding and wheat filling the storehouse; it does not supply the patronymic.
Zakut uses examples of titles and allows both incomplete ordination and a teacher’s informal address.
